verdict.rationale: Semgrep's docs have a dedicated pre-commit page stating the pre-commit framework can run semgrep on commit to keep secrets and security issues out of Git history. Local scans need no login and code is not uploaded by default, which suits a local hook, and Semgrep Secrets covers credential detection. Missing for 10: hook configuration details (e.g. the .pre-commit-config.yaml entry or staged-file scoping), confirmation that Semgrep Secrets' validated detection runs inside the hook, and independent hands-on corroboration of pre-commit use.
